subject: french
title: Regional Variation
welcome_lead: French varies by region. Belgian, Swiss, Quebecois and African French each carry distinctive vocabulary and pronunciation.
meta_desc: French: regional variations across the French-speaking world.
final_note: There is no single French — only Frenches.

concepts.def: Quebec French — distinctive vowels and vocab.
African French — shaped by contact languages.
French slang where syllables are inverted (e.g. ouf = fou).

walkthroughs.body_html: France: soixante-dix, quatre-vingts, quatre-vingt-dix. Belgium: septante, quatre-vingts, nonante. Switzerland: septante, huitante, nonante.
Femme > meuf; fete > teuf; arabe > beur. Verlan emerges from the banlieues — be careful with register.
Quebecois uses old French features: nasal vowels are tighter, tu often used informally where France uses vous.
